_what: The seven channel-change flights of the house pigeon, generated in Higgsfield on 2026-10-05 at the owner's instruction ("use higgsfield to make a 4k better pigeon flying transition"; "4-5 is good of varying lengths but our mascot needs to be consistent in look"; "you can have 5-7 transitions ... lean more in to the flamboyance"; "real pigeon movements like twirling in air and pigeon showmanship"). Masters, start frames and the empty end frame are owner-local under output/Higgsfield Assets/Khajistan Flights 2026-10-05/. Every start frame was made with gpt_image_2_5 (4K, quality high) from the house reference Pigeon-Reference-4K.jpg on a flat grey (RGB 140) backdrop; every flight ends on the empty grey frame so the bird must leave the shot.

across.note: the website's wing wipe, remade: diagonally across and into the lens, a wing fills the frame, exits top right

twirl.role: change (fitted to the tune time) and wait
twirl.note: the owner's flamboyant swirling crossing, for a long tune

roller.role: change (fitted to the tune time) and wait
roller.note: a Birmingham roller's backward somersaults, wings raised, tumbling like a spinning ball, then away

spiral.role: change (fitted to the tune time) and wait

display.role: change (fitted to the tune time) and wait
display.note: display flight: slow exaggerated wing-claps over the back, a hover with the tail fanned, then across

wing.note: Across's start frame; flies into the lens and ends with the wing over 97% of the frame. The channel cuts in behind it (rendered with 'covered': nothing trimmed or faded, a backdrop plate per frame). Owner, 2026-10-05: 'a wing covering the full screen'. The pink feet show for about four frames near the lens.

refused.kling3_0 4k twirl fd6cc694, swoop 5ae403: smoke-like smears behind the wings, a bird frozen in place for 1.5 s, and a body twisted into an S (spiral). Kling 3.0 renders straight flight well and acrobatics badly.
refused.kling3_0 4k across af0ec211, approach 65: wings held still through most of the shot; the kept takes beat.
refused.kling3_0 4k roller 62dc5723-1e07-4795-86: frozen for its first four frames, then the 'roll' is a smear of the wings on a bird that keeps its side-on pose.
refused.kling3_0 4k display be25ae06-e810-450f-8: ghosted, doubled wings in its third and fourth seconds.
refused.seedance_2_5 roller 536c8539-3d87-4be9-a: a sound roll but the second take (kept) tumbles in place, as a roller does; this one is not refused for a defect and is the spare.
refused.kling3_0 4k approach 17459310-82fa-4034-: asked for a sharp close pass over the lens; both hover and fly up and away, never coming nearer than 10% of the frame.
refused.kling3_0 4k across b0ec2b84, approach c9: out of focus whenever the bird is near the lens: bird sharpness fell from ~250 to ~5 over the last 1.5 s of each. Owner: 'the feathers get pixelated and blurry'. Remade in Seedance, which keeps feather barbs at its closest.
refused.seedance_2_5 across 44d10e93-ca0c-4297-9: never comes nearer than 11% of the frame: not the 'into us' flight.
refused.seedance_2_5 approach 49abda56-b528-4569: fills two-thirds of the frame and lingers there.

credits: 1726.75 in all, measured off the Higgsfield balance: 1821.5 at the start; 154.75 after the refused cover flights; 94.75 after the Wing take (2026-10-06).
pipeline: render_flight.py: per-pixel backdrop plate (whichever of end-frames median and flight median is closer to neutral grey), alpha = (C-B).(F-B)/|F-B|^2 with F spread from the solid bird, colourless shadows dropped, colour premultiplied, Seedance plumage Lab-matched to the Kling bird (colour.json, gain capped 1.5); the generator's slow opening retimed to half the clip's median pace (at most 3x) and a close pass over the lens (bird over 60% of the frame, out of focus) at 3x; tail cut where the bird stops moving, a still-on-edge ending faded over 6 frames. Laid on each skin's ground and encoded opaque: H.264 1080 for every flight, HEVC 2160 from a 4K source. HEVC with alpha was dropped 2026-10-05: the Apple TV HD decodes it in software and lost frames while a channel tuned.

swoop.why: owner, 2026-10-05: "looks like it's swimming and seems 2d"

rise.note: climbs away from the camera, wings clapped over the back in a raised V: a pigeon's display climb
rise.why: owner, 2026-10-05: "i dont like the one that is showing the back and going up"

approach.note: straight at the camera, passes over it
approach.why: owner, 2026-10-06: the feet, head-on toward the camera, 'too ugly'

refused_cover_flights.what: seven Seedance flights that opened and closed on one 4K image of the wing filling the frame (cover image 4a5d0fce-baa2-4517-b339-12c36ef844e1), chained wing to wing and fitted to each channel's tune time. Shipped to the TV as ff8c79b88 on 2026-10-06 and reverted the same night.
refused_cover_flights.owner: 'this most recent one is bad': the full-screen wing looked fake/static; the bird too small and far once it pulled back; glitchy; 'the speed is unrealistic, it needs to be more like the original' (the two darts played at 1.8x).
refused_cover_flights.lesson: do not speed a generated flight up to fit a time: the wingbeat speeds up with it and reads as fake. A generated still image as the cover frame reads as a still, not as the bird.

playback: Every frame at the speed it was generated (owner, 2026-10-06: 'the speed is unrealistic'). The change flight is the shortest that outlasts the channel's expected tune time (TuneTimes, measured per channel on the device), turning among those within a second of it.
